summary: Retested the iteration_36 fixes and the new SKHY / foreign-listing scaling. What works: the regression suites pass 62/62 (unit + iter38 + iter39). SKHY quick endpoint returns available=true, 9 methods, listing_scale 0.000120, value $627.71 vs price $164.70, confidence low with a caution note. The full long-term analysis gives the same OptiIQ value. TSM listing_scale is 0.183. AAPL, PLTR, V and UBER are 1.0. NVO (0.148) and TM (0.068) also look right. Warm quick calls for AAPL, PLTR and JPM take 0.2-0.4s. JPM skips the 4 cash-flow methods. Board list values match the quick endpoint. The optiiq_board refill is running: 382 -> 398 -> 411 -> 414 of 503 over about 9 minutes (about 4/min, slowed by auto-reloads). PLTR is on the board. V and UBER are not in the collection yet (refill pending), but their quick values are fine. Frontend: the SKHY quick card shows in 0.83s with the caution text and optiiq-listing-note; the full card shows the same $627.71. The note does not show for AAPL or PLTR. The COST -> ADBE (board sheet) race is fixed: COST's full result at +6.5s was ignored, the ADBE quick card stayed, and ADBE's full result came at +10.1s. NEW BUGS: (1) SKHY's full long-term card still uses unscaled Korean-won figures everywhere outside the OptiIQ card: EPS (TTM) $227,607.99, scenarios Bull $8,024,238 / weighted $6,302,101 (+3,826,312%), buy/sell point $4.66M/$8.02M, market cap $977T, EPS estimate $99,667, 52-week high 2,987,000, and the AI thesis remarks that the EPS looks like another currency. (2) listing_scale gives false positives on US stocks IBKR (0.264) and CVNA (0.255). Their per-share figures get shrunk about 4x and the 'reported in another currency' note shows for a US stock. No deprecated Expo packages found.

critical.endpoint: POST /api/screener/stock-analysis (purpose=long) for foreign listings (SKHY, TSM etc.)
critical.issue: listing_scale is only applied inside optiiq_of. server.py:859-885 uses the raw metrics for eps_ttm, pe-based dcf_valuation (scenarios, buy_point, sell_point), earnings_eps_estimate, fifty_two_week_high/low, valuation_measures.market_cap/enterprise_value and the AI prompt (EPS $227607). For SKHY that means weighted value $6.3M, buy point $4,657,807.84, EPS $227,607.99, market cap $977.41T, all shown on the Analyze long card.

US listings get k != 1. IBKR: pe_ttm 120.9 x eps 2.61 = 316 vs price 83.54, so k=0.264. ps x rps and pb x bvps agree, which means the provider's ratio fields are stale (pre-split) while the per-share figures are already in listing terms (market_cap 142.3B / price = 1.70B shares, which is IBKR's share count). EPS without NRI ends up $0.69, CVNA operating cash flow $286M (its filings show net income $310M in one quarter), and the UI shows the 'another currency / home-market share' note on US stocks. CVNA and IBKR are on the board with these wrong values (IBKR shown as very_under).

minor.issue: financials_source is hard-coded to 'SEC 10-Q/10-K filings via Finnhub' even when financials is [] (SKHY, TSM have no SEC quarterly rows).

minor.endpoint: optiiq_for (SKHY/TSM/other foreign tickers without SEC financials)
minor.issue: Results are never saved to optiiq_inputs because doc['financials'] is empty (server.py:742). Each quick lookup after the market cache expires costs 5 Finnhub calls again, so foreign tickers are not 'efficient' like US ones.

minor.endpoint: optiiq method notes for scaled listings
minor.issue: Note totals like 'Operating cash flow $15.23B' or 'Net income $19.42B' for SKHY are home-currency totals multiplied by the per-listing price factor. They are not real USD company totals, which can mislead users. Consider showing per-share figures only, or labelling them.
Currency gaps under 2x are never corrected (EUR, GBP, CHF, CAD, AUD reporters such as ASML get k=1.0). Values can be 10-35% off for those ADRs.

Refill is about 4.5 stocks/min. At 414/503 the last ~89 (including UBER and V) need about 20 more minutes. Every backend auto-reload (any file change under /app/backend, including tests) loses the lease and pauses the refill for up to 3 min.

ui_bugs.issue: SKHY shows absurd unscaled values: scenario cards $8024238.39 / $6263180.82 / $4657807.84 that overflow their card width, Probability-weighted value $6302101.97 (+3826312.9%), Buy/Sell point $4.66M/$8.02M, Market Cap $977.41T, EPS (TTM) $227607.99, EPS estimate $99667.28. Root cause is backend (see critical #1).
optiiq-listing-note shows for US stock IBKR in the board sheet (caused by the listing_scale false positive).

issues: Scenario card value text has no adjustsFontSizeToFit/numberOfLines, so large values overflow into neighbouring cards

action_items: stock_analysis (server.py ~853-899): compute k = listing_scale(price, metrics) once. Scale eps_ttm, earnings eps_estimate, 52w high/low (or hide them when k != 1), and the eps passed to dcf_valuation (or skip the EPS-DCF editor for k != 1). Scale or label market_cap/EV as home currency, and pass the scaled EPS to the AI prompt.

listing_scale: don't trigger on US listings with stale provider ratios. Options: only apply when profile country != 'US' or the reporting currency != USD; or cross-check market_cap / price against the share count from the SEC filings (IBKR 1.70B matches, so k should be 1); or prefer the per-share figures when SEC financials exist. Add IBKR and CVNA to the unit tests as k == 1 cases.
Set financials_source to a 'no SEC filings for this listing' text when financials is empty.
Optionally cache optiiq inputs for no-financials foreign tickers (metrics-only doc) so SKHY/TSM quick lookups don't spend 5 Finnhub calls each time.
Recheck later that the board reaches ~500 and that UBER and V appear in GET /api/valuation/board stocks.
critical_code_review_comments: optiiq.py:55-65 listing_scale picks the first ratio pair available and trusts it. A stale P/E (split, restatement) on a US stock triggers scaling. It needs a sanity cross-check across ratio pairs and against filing share counts.
server.py:859-885 mixes scaled (optiiq) and unscaled (eps/valuation/measures) numbers in one response, so the card contradicts itself for foreign listings.
analyze.tsx run(): the lastRun guard is now correct for setData, setLoading and toast (verified live).
market.get_profile no longer caches empty answers (market.py:283). The budget warning log is present.

success_rate.backend: 13/16 iter40 tests (3 failures are real bugs) + 62/62 regression = 75/78 (96%)
success_rate.frontend: 90% (quick card, listing note, parity, race fix and board sheet work; SKHY full card shows unscaled figures; IBKR note false positive)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=https://optionscope.preview.emergentagent.com python -m pytest tests/test_iter40_listing_scale_board.py -q -s -n0 (pytest.ini adds -n xdist; use -n0 for ordered output). The backend DB is SHARED_DB_NAME via atlas.shared_mongo_url, not MONGO_URL/DB_NAME. Board docs are in optiiq_board; lease is locks.board_refresh. Creating or editing test files under /app/backend triggers uvicorn reload and pauses the board refill.
rca_of_issue: SKHY full card: optiiq_of applies listing_scale to its own copy of the metrics, but stock_analysis builds eps/valuation/measures from the raw metrics, so only the OptiIQ block is converted. IBKR/CVNA: listing_scale = price/(pe_ttm*eps_ttm). Finnhub's pe/ps/pb for these tickers imply a price ~4x the quote (stale pre-split ratios), so a US stock is treated as a foreign listing. Repro: GET /api/valuation/optiiq/IBKR -> inputs.listing_scale 0.264; POST /api/screener/stock-analysis {ticker:SKHY,purpose:long} -> eps_ttm 227607.99, buy_point 4657807.84.
